PAPERS.short: Manchanda hyperlocal BC sensing Bayesian inverse modeling West Oakland 2026
PAPERS.title: Hyperlocal sensing and inverse modeling reveal community impacts of urban air pollutant emissions
PAPERS.pm: Black carbon from dense fixed-site network (6.7 sites/km2) plus mobile mapping
PAPERS.endpoint: Hourly 150 m BC emission maps; population-weighted exposure attribution
PAPERS.n: Dense mobile and fixed-site BC measurements were assimilated in a Bayesian inversion to produce hourly 150 x 150 m emission maps for West Oakland, a freight-corridor community. The posterior raised total BC emissions by ~33% over the bottom-up inventory and quadrupled the share of population-weighted exposure attributed to neighbourhood and port-related sources (5% to 20%), concentrated in low-income blocks. Sensitivity runs with ~10 fixed monitors (~1 site/km2) plus time-averaged mobile maps recovered similar results. Limitation: the posterior is only as good as the transport kernel and prior error covariance; unpermitted sources are inferred, not verified on the ground, and one community limits transfer. Relevance: high - a direct recipe for turning a sparse low-cost BC/PM network into source-resolved emission corrections.

PAPERS.short: Baliaka Eaton urban firestorm airborne toxic metals lead Los Angeles 2026
PAPERS.title: Fire at the boundary: Airborne toxic metals from the 2025 Los Angeles urban firestorm
PAPERS.pm: Real-time airborne trace elements (XRF) in PM during the Eaton fire
PAPERS.endpoint: Plume metal enrichment vs wildfire smoke; population exposure to 24-h lead
PAPERS.n: Hourly airborne trace-element measurements during the January 2025 Eaton fire tracked the transition from structure to wildland burning via the K/Pb ratio. Relative to wildfire smoke, the urban plume was enriched >50-fold in lead, ~7-fold in halogens and ~3-fold in arsenic, attributed to vehicles, electronics and building materials. An estimated 7 million residents (range 4.3-8.0 million) experienced 24-h lead above 50 ng/m3, >80 times background. Limitation: population exposure is extrapolated from a small number of monitoring points through a dispersion estimate, and the 24-h lead threshold has no health-based standard counterpart (NAAQS is a 3-month mean). Relevance: high - optical PM sensors would register the smoke but not its metal toxicity; speciation is needed.

PAPERS.short: Luglio air pollution pediatric asthma hospitalizations Louisiana vulnerable groups 2026
PAPERS.title: Associations between air pollution and pediatric asthma hospitalizations across vulnerable groups in Louisiana
PAPERS.pm: Daily PM2.5, O3 and NO2 (NO2 2010-2016 only)
PAPERS.endpoint: Pediatric (<18 y) asthma hospitalizations
PAPERS.n: 28,499 asthma hospitalizations in children in Louisiana 2010-2019, time-stratified case-crossover with DLNM to lag 3. Cumulative lag 0-3: PM2.5 OR 1.079 (1.052-1.107), O3 1.082 (1.050-1.116), NO2 1.071 (1.034-1.111), with increments as defined in the paper. In multipollutant models O3 and NO2 attenuated while PM2.5 persisted. Effect modification by race and Medicaid status was not significant, although lag patterns differed (lags 1-2 Black children, lag 3 White children). Limitation: exposure assigned from area-level estimates in a state with sparse monitoring outside the industrial corridor, so differential misclassification by race/rurality could mask modification; NO2 covers only 2010-2016. Relevance: medium - higher-burden groups sit where reference coverage is thinnest.

PAPERS.short: Andreotti active fire detections circulatory hospital admissions Brazil ecological panel 2026
PAPERS.title: Active Fire Detections and Hospital Admissions for Circulatory Diseases in Brazil: An Ecological Panel Study (2013-2024)
PAPERS.pm: Annual satellite active-fire detection density (INPE) as smoke proxy
PAPERS.endpoint: Hospital admissions for ICD-10 chapter IX circulatory diseases
PAPERS.n: 27 Brazilian federative units x 12 years (324 unit-years), 13.8 million circulatory admissions and 2.3 million fire detections. Correlations were null (rho -0.03 to 0.01). In negative-binomial models with state fixed effects, year effects, temperature, poverty and primary-care coverage, the rate ratio per additional 1,000 detections/100,000 km2/year was 0.998 (0.970-1.028), null in every subset and with clustered SEs. Limitation: annual state-level fire counts are far removed from short-term smoke PM2.5 at residence; smoke from Amazon fires is exported to other states, so the exposure is misplaced as well as aggregated. The authors correctly state this is not evidence of no effect. Relevance: low - illustrates why fire counts cannot substitute for measured PM.

PAPERS.short: Duan landscape fire-sourced PM2.5 kidney function eGFR children China 2026
PAPERS.title: Landscape fire-sourced PM2.5 and kidney function in children: evidence from a national cross-sectional study in China
PAPERS.pm: Three-year mean landscape fire-sourced PM2.5 at school address (modelled)
PAPERS.endpoint: eGFR from serum creatinine, ages 5-18
PAPERS.n: China National Nutrition and Health Surveillance of Children and Lactating Women 2016-2018, n=12,102 aged 5-18. Per IQR (0.505 ug/m3) of fire-sourced PM2.5: eGFR -0.83 mL/min/1.73 m2 (-1.03 to -0.62); middle-school students -1.46 (-1.83 to -1.09) vs primary -0.59 (-0.84 to -0.34). Associations were stronger with low NDVI and low vitamin or carbohydrate intake. Limitation: an IQR of 0.5 ug/m3 is a tiny contrast for an effect this size, which points to residual spatial confounding (fire-PM tracks rural, agricultural regions); creatinine-based eGFR in children depends on muscle mass and hydration, which also vary by region. Cross-sectional. Relevance: low - source-specific PM from a chemical-transport model, no sensing.

PAPERS.short: Zhu prenatal PM1 PM2.5 PM10 childhood hemoglobin anemia Fujian birth cohort 2026
PAPERS.title: Association of prenatal PM1, PM2.5, and PM10 exposure with early childhood hemoglobin levels and anemia: Identification of susceptibility windows
PAPERS.pm: Trimester-specific PM1, PM2.5, PM10 (ChinaHighAirPollutants)
PAPERS.endpoint: Early-childhood hemoglobin and anemia
PAPERS.n: Fujian Birth Cohort paediatric subcohort, 1,235 mother-child pairs. Per 1 ug/m3 over the whole pregnancy, child hemoglobin fell by 1.02 (0.53-1.52) for PM1, 0.87 (0.46-1.28) for PM2.5 and 0.37 (0.19-0.56) for PM10 (units as reported). First-trimester anemia ORs per unit were 1.23, 1.16 and 1.09; DLMs placed the hemoglobin window in early-mid pregnancy and the anemia window in the first trimester. Limitation: per-microgram effects of this size imply implausibly large decrements across the cohort's range; PM1, PM2.5 and PM10 are near-collinear satellite products, so the size-fraction ranking is not interpretable. Postnatal exposure and diet are not stated. Relevance: low - satellite-derived exposures only.

PAPERS.short: Wang air pollutants sleep apnea polysomnography architecture Shenzhen 2026
PAPERS.title: Associations of multiple ambient air pollutants and sleep apnea, sleep architecture and nocturnal oxygenation in adult patients with or without obstructive sleep apnea (OSA)
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5, PM10, PM2.5 inorganic components, NO2, SO2, CO, O3; lag 0-180 d
PAPERS.endpoint: OSA severity (AHI), sleep stages, nocturnal oxygenation (polysomnography)
PAPERS.n: Retrospective polysomnography study of 4,049 adults in Shenzhen. Over a 0-180 day lag window, PM2.5, PM10, NO2, SO2, CO and diurnal temperature range were associated with greater OSA severity. PM2.5 and PM10 were associated with 1.71% and 1.32% of total sleep time more N1 and 1.51% and 1.32% less N3 sleep (increments as reported). O3 and DTR showed the clearest associations with oxygenation; PM2.5 had a rising exposure-response. Limitation: the lag window was chosen post hoc, which inflates false-positive risk across many pollutant-outcome pairs; a clinic-referred sample means referral itself may track season and pollution. CIs are not given in the abstract. Relevance: low - city-level exposure.

PAPERS.short: Cao PM2.5 chemical components heart disease longitudinal China 123 cities 2026
PAPERS.title: Association between PM2.5 and its chemical components exposure and heart disease risk: a longitudinal study from China
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 and components (SO4, NO3, NH4, OM, BC), gridded
PAPERS.endpoint: Incident heart disease
PAPERS.n: 8,172 participants from 123 Chinese cities; Cox models with three adjustment levels plus WQS mixtures. Per 1 ug/m3 PM2.5: HR 1.027 (1.022-1.032); BC had the largest per-unit estimate, HR 1.381 (1.266-1.506). All components showed non-linear exposure-response; southern residents and overweight participants had stronger associations; PAF 2.63%. Limitation: per-ug/m3 component HRs are not comparable because component ranges differ by an order of magnitude, and components are highly collinear, so 'BC largest' is a scaling artefact unless expressed per IQR. Heart disease is likely self-reported (cohort not named in the abstract). Relevance: medium - again points to absorption (BC) as the health-relevant channel.

PAPERS.short: Wang air pollution adolescent anxiety depression Sichuan cross-sectional 2026
PAPERS.title: Air pollution and mental health in adolescents: a cross-sectional study in Sichuan, China
PAPERS.pm: PM10, PM2.5, O3, CO, SO2, NO2 assigned via IP-geolocated survey location; winter periods
PAPERS.endpoint: PHQ-9 depression and GAD-7 anxiety (score >=5), ages 10-19
PAPERS.n: 71,364 school students aged 10-19, surveyed over two winters (2022-23, 2023-24). Per IQR, PM10 anxiety OR 1.29 (1.22-1.36) and O3 1.24 (1.19-1.29), with similar depression associations; a weighted combined score rose stepwise. PM2.5 and SO2 were inversely associated. Limitation: exposure was assigned from the IP address of the online survey, i.e. a point-in-time location of the device, and the PM10-positive/PM2.5-inverse split from highly correlated pollutants is the signature of collinearity and spatial confounding rather than a fraction-specific effect. Relevance: low - coarse exposure assignment.

PAPERS.short: Hu air pollution built environment lung cancer recurrence after surgery China 2026
PAPERS.title: Ambient Air Pollution, Residential Built Environment, and Lung Cancer Recurrence After Curative-Intent Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study in Three Chinese Cities
PAPERS.pm: Satellite-derived 1 km PM2.5, PM10, NO2, CO, SO2, O3 (post-diagnosis first year)
PAPERS.endpoint: Tumour recurrence after curative-intent lung cancer resection
PAPERS.n: 542 adults after curative resection at three tertiary hospitals (2019-2026); 60 recurrences, median follow-up 27.3 months. Site-stratified meta-analysis, per within-site SD of first-year post-diagnosis exposure: PM2.5 HR 1.41 (1.08-1.84), PM10 1.38 (1.10-1.73), NO2 1.67, CO 1.51, SO2 1.59; O3 null. A co-exposure component gave HR 1.51 (1.20-1.89); green-space diversity HR 0.59/SD. Limitation: 60 events across six pollutants, mixtures and built-environment terms is badly underpowered for adjustment; within-site SD contrasts are small and residence tracks stage, histology and access to follow-up imaging. Preprint. Relevance: low.

PAPERS.short: Valuvunina PM2.5 PurpleAir quarry low birth weight Kinshasa DRC 2026
PAPERS.title: Atmospheric Pollution by Fine Particulate Matter (PM2.5) and Low Birth Weight: A Cross-Sectional Study in Binza Ozone Health Zone, Democratic Republic of the Congo, 2022
PAPERS.pm: Calibrated PurpleAir PA-II-SD PM2.5 (48-72 h per health area; 0.52 x raw + 3.2 vs BAM)
PAPERS.endpoint: Low birth weight (<2500 g)
PAPERS.n: 355 mothers delivering in 2021 at six facilities near the Carrigres quarry. LBW prevalence 12.96% (9.7-16.9). PurpleAir PA-II-SD sensors, corrected with a Kinshasa BAM-derived equation, gave area PM2.5 54.6-102.5 ug/m3. Residence <500 m from the quarry: aOR 4.12 (1.98-8.57); area PM2.5 >75 ug/m3: aOR 1.18 (0.59-2.36). Limitation: PM2.5 was measured for 48-72 h in 2022 and assigned to births in 2021, i.e. after the pregnancies, at the health-area level, so the null PM2.5 result says nothing about gestational exposure; quarry dust is coarse and poorly captured by Plantower optics. Relevance: high - a direct example of low-cost sensors used as the sole exposure metric, and of the temporal mismatch that undermines it.

PAPERS.short: Kusumaningtiar school children PM2.5 PM10 health risk systematic review 2026
PAPERS.title: Environmental Health Risks in School Children Due to Air Pollution Exposure: Systematic Literature Review
PAPERS.pm: Indoor and outdoor school PM2.5 and PM10
PAPERS.endpoint: Respiratory health risk (risk quotient, lung function, MPPD deposition)
PAPERS.n: PRISMA review (PROSPERO CRD420261282406) of 12 studies published 2015-2025 on school PM2.5 and PM10, combining environmental health risk assessment, epidemiology, MPPD dosimetry and STELLA modelling. Several studies reported risk quotients >1; one Bandung study found inverse PM2.5-lung function associations; dosimetry indicated higher airway deposition in children. Limitation: 12 heterogeneous studies with mixed methods and no quantitative synthesis; RQ>1 depends on default intake assumptions rather than measured outcomes. Preprint. Relevance: medium - underlines the need for standardised school-level monitoring that low-cost networks could provide.

PAPERS.short: Nored lithium-ion battery fire soot PM pulmonary toxicity mice fluoride 2026
PAPERS.title: Pulmonary Toxicity of Particulate-Phase Combustion Byproducts from Lithium-Ion Battery Fires
PAPERS.pm: LIB thermal-runaway soot and smoke PM (<10 um), chemical composition
PAPERS.endpoint: Lung inflammation and pulmonary function in mice, 4 h and 24 h
PAPERS.n: Soot (10 fire tests) and smoke PM (2 tests) from lithium-ion battery thermal runaway were size-filtered to <10 um and given to mice (100 ug). Soot had more carbon (37% vs 18%), PM more anions (12% vs 6%), inorganic elements similar (23-28%); particulate fluoride reached ~5% of mass. Only soot altered ventilatory timing, peak expiratory flow and relaxation time; both raised lung inflammation to levels comparable with other combustion sources. Fluoride, Al, Fe, Ni and Li were associated with toxicity. Limitation: a single 100 ug bolus (aspiration/instillation) is not inhalation dosimetry, two smoke tests is a thin basis, and component-toxicity associations across so few samples are exploratory. Relevance: low - toxicology; flags fluoride-bearing PM as a new indoor/urban fire hazard.

PAPERS.short: Lian firework barium aerosols single-particle SPAMS Guangzhou 2026
PAPERS.title: Evolution of firework-related barium aerosols: insights from single-particle analysis and mass concentration monitoring
PAPERS.pm: Online Ba mass concentration plus single-particle aerosol mass spectrometry (SPAMS)
PAPERS.endpoint: Firework Ba peaks and Ba-particle ageing classes
PAPERS.n: Online Ba mass monitoring and SPAMS at four Guangzhou sites through firework events. Ba rose 1-3 orders of magnitude above background. The urban-core site under a complete firework ban peaked lower than a suburban site with time- and place-restricted use, despite higher population density - consistent with, but not proof of, a ban effect. Chloride-rich and nitrate-dominated Ba-containing particle classes were interpreted as fresh and aged, tracking chloride displacement and nitrate uptake. Limitation: four sites and a few events; the ban contrast is confounded by local emissions and transport, as the authors acknowledge, and SPAMS is semi-quantitative. Relevance: medium - firework episodes are a known optical-sensor artefact (hygroscopic, metal-rich particles), and this characterises their chemistry.

PAPERS.short: Wei PM2.5 ozone nonlinear coupling Puyang oilfield city GAM 2015-2025 2026
PAPERS.title: Long-Term Trends and Nonlinear PM2.5-O3 Coupling in a Typical Oilfield City of the "2 + 26" Region
PAPERS.pm: Daily PM2.5 and MDA8 O3 (fixed monitors), 2015-2025
PAPERS.endpoint: Concentration-stratified PM2.5-O3 correlation; GAM partial effects
PAPERS.n: Daily PM2.5 and MDA8 O3 in Puyang 2015-2025 with nested GAMs adding meteorology, NO2, humidity and season interactions. Raw correlation reversed by concentration band: r 0.271 below 35 ug/m3, -0.208 at 35-75 and -0.313 above 75. After controlling for meteorology and NO2, the conditional partial effect of PM2.5 on O3 increased over most of the range, so the negative raw correlation is largely meteorological. The low-band positive coupling strengthened over time (0.190 to 0.306). Limitation: one city, observational correlations; GAM partial effects do not identify chemical mechanisms (aerosol radiative or heterogeneous HO2 uptake). Relevance: low.

PAPERS.short: Zhao spin-trapping EPR radicals atmospheric fine particulate matter cavity quality factor 2026
PAPERS.title: Optimized spin-trapping method for radicals detection induced by atmospheric fine particulate matter: Critical roles of temporal evolution and cavity quality factor
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5-induced radicals (EPR spin trapping)
PAPERS.endpoint: Radical detection method optimisation
PAPERS.n: Title and authors only (Zhao, Chen, Ding, Zhang et al.); no abstract retrievable from Crossref, Europe PMC or Semantic Scholar at harvest. The title describes optimising EPR spin-trapping for radicals generated by PM2.5, identifying the time course of adduct formation and the cavity quality factor as critical. Sample type, n and performance metrics cannot be stated. Limitation: unverifiable beyond the title; spin-trap adducts decay on minute timescales, so inter-lab oxidative-potential comparisons hinge on exactly these timing choices. Relevance: low - offline oxidative-potential metrology.

PAPERS.short: Kulmala determination deposition rates indoor particle dynamics 2026
PAPERS.title: Determination of deposition rates from indoor particle dynamics
PAPERS.pm: Indoor particle concentration decay (size-resolved, presumed)
PAPERS.geo: Finland (inferred from author affiliation; not stated in record)
PAPERS.endpoint: Indoor particle deposition rates
PAPERS.n: Title and authors only (Kulmala I., Siilin, Hakala, Ehder-Gahm); no abstract retrievable at harvest. The title describes deriving particle deposition rates from indoor concentration dynamics. Method, size range and validation cannot be stated. Limitation: unverifiable beyond the title; decay-based deposition estimates are confounded by air-exchange and mixing assumptions unless these are measured independently. Relevance: medium - deposition rates are an input for indoor/outdoor ratio models used to interpret paired indoor and outdoor low-cost sensors.

PAPERS.short: Ng particulate matter respiratory deposition inhalation dose biomass burning homes indigenous communities 2026
PAPERS.title: Particulate Matter Exposure, Respiratory Deposition and Inhalation Dosage Assessment in Biomass Burning Homes in Rural Indigenous Communities
PAPERS.pm: Household PM from biomass burning; respiratory deposition / inhaled dose
PAPERS.geo: India (inferred from author affiliation; not stated in record)
PAPERS.endpoint: Respiratory-tract deposition and inhaled dose
PAPERS.n: Title and authors only (Ng, Monalisa, Balachandran, Hoque et al.); day-0 Elsevier deposit with no abstract at harvest. The title describes household PM measurement in biomass-burning homes in rural indigenous communities with respiratory deposition and inhaled-dose modelling. Instruments, n and concentrations cannot be stated. Limitation: unverifiable beyond the title; deposition models (e.g. MPPD) are sensitive to the assumed size distribution, which optical monitors in smoke-laden kitchens report poorly. Relevance: medium - household biomass smoke is a key use case for low-cost PM monitors.

PAPERS.title: On-road emissions of light-duty vehicles: detailed analysis of particulate and gaseous pollutants
PAPERS.pm: Light-duty vehicle on-road particulate and gaseous emissions
PAPERS.geo: France (inferred from author affiliation; not stated in record)

PAPERS.title: Metal distribution in atmospheric particulate matter (PM2.5) from urban areas with smelting activities in the Rio de Janeiro state, Brazil: Solubility, correlation and risk assessment

PAPERS.short: Pani Southeast Asian biomass burning smoke aerosol light extinction apportionment high-altitude western North Pacific 2026
PAPERS.title: Impact of peninsular Southeast Asian biomass-burning smoke on chemical apportionment of aerosol light extinction at a high-altitude remote environment in the western North Pacific
